title: The start of something new
summary:
A twisted fate awaited the party as they awoke amidst the rubble of what had once been the Silver Chalice. Shattered beams and broken stone told the story of sudden destruction, the work of a young dragon, its mind possessed by chaos.

Within moments, Waess noticed something was wrong. The dragon was sick. Without hesitation, he chose survival over confrontation, setting his sights on escape and rushing to bring himself to safety.

Ray, however, had other plans. Spotting a seemingly injured figure lying helplessly on the ground, he shot an arrow at the dragon, successfully drawing its attention away from the victim. 
The dragon’s gaze shifted and then it noticed Waess attempting to flee.

With a powerful beat of its wings, the dragon took off and struck Waess down, knocking him unconscious. Ray sprinted toward Waess’s fallen body, desperately trying to check on him. He placed himself between Waess's unconscious body and the dragon, standing as a shield.

The dragon struck Ray with the same brutal force, leaving him collpased on the ground beside Waess.

Amidst the chaos, Marvers focused on what he could still save. He moved through the wreckage, helping as many survivors as possible. His efforts failed at the last person, a woman with a broken leg, barely able to suppress her pain filled whimpers.

The dragon quickly noticed.

It lunged toward Marvers and sank its teeth into his shoulder, attempting to finish him off right where he stood.

“Just when it seems that all hope is lost, the three of you feel a sudden warmth, a resonance within the items that have guided your journey so far. Light bursts from each of your "special" items. Marvers’s holy symbol, Ray’s bolotie and Waess’s moon necklace. You begin to float off the ground, the light swirling around you, merging into a blinding magical explosion that shakes the Inn to its foundations.”

Everyone wakes up in the Monastery located on the very top of Guardians Height.

Waess and Ray talked things out regarding the attack right after they awoke, while Marvers checked on Martin and his newly found friend. Martin, worried, asked Marvers to find out whether his grandmother Lilia was safe.

Afterward, Waess struck up a conversation with Aarely. And through him, Marvers discovered that they shared the same religion.

Ray headed to the Main Hall to speak with Berta, a nun who lived in the monastery, about the deity Talona and this mysterious Person called Misha. During their conversation, he learned that Talona has an active temple in Duweil. Berta sent a messenger to a priest who was close to Misha to gather more information about her whereabouts.

Meanwhile, Marvers and Waess went to a small and diy'd temple (probably by Aarley) to pray to Soldea. Both of them individually prayed, received a subtle sign in response and then left. On their way back, Waess discovered a small note from Wilfen, written in Elvish using expensive purple ink. "Whoever can read this, Hello there :)"

Later, Ray went to the gardens by himself to inform Erwin (in his head) that everything was alright. While there, he too received a small sign making him feel assured that he is going to be alright, everything is going to be alright..

title: Leaving Guardians Height behind
summary:
The group found themselves still within the monastery. After Ray briefly left Waess and Marvers to explore the gardens, the two decided to further inspect the murals lining the monastery’s walls. Marvers noticed several explicit sexual depictions, including one portraying the three rulers of Lacrima, Duweil and Dredel engaged in intercourse, accompanied by an elvish inscription reading “Fuck Capitalism.” Marvers was deeply confused as to why such imagery was permitted on holy grounds.

Meanwhile, Waess cast Redraw and Rewrite, causing the letters of Wiltfen’s message to dance and transform into small, stick-like figures. He also commented that Marvers’ “Spine tale”, an element of Ivian culture seemed unusually short for his age. Marvers bluntly shut the conversation down, making it clear he did not wish to discuss it.

When Ray returned, he and Waess set off together with two goals: to find Aarely and to get Ray to a post office. On their way toward the monastery’s main entrance, the two shared a surprisingly intimate conversation, ending in Waess offering himself should Ray ever wish to explore intimacy with another man. The moment was abruptly interrupted by a passing monk. They asked him for directions to Aarely and the post office, then parted ways.

While this was happening, Marvers returned to the room left to where they had first awakened. After knocking, he heard a hushed “enter”and slowly opened the door to complete darkness. As he stepped inside, the door slammed shut behind him and a hand gripped his shoulder, startling him. Once his eyes adjusted, he saw a tall high elf, nearly his height, standing close behind him.

The elf seized Marvers arm and pulled him toward the altar, where he cast light on a wooden handle and pointed to a book. He wrote a single question: "What are you looking for?” Upon closer inspection, Marvers noticed how unsettling the elf appeared, long, straight black hair perfectly arranged down his back, a slim face, and a prominent scar running across his left eye. One eye was milky white, the other a piercing grey.

After a brief interaction, the elf guided Marvers out of the room, still holding his hand. As they left, Marvers caught a glimpse of someone lying in the darkness, a person with a fatal looking wound that did not bleed. Instead, the injury appeared grown over with grey, ashen wood. The figure made no sound, yet Marvers was convinced they were still alive. Shaken, he paused to steady himself before continuing his search for Layla.

Elsewhere, Waess found Aarely and pulled him out of an impending burnout by guilting him into joining Waess for a meal. They sat down at a small restaurant consisting of a bar counter and three tables, where they ate Meadowroot and Griftlon stew, a dish similar to one from Lacrima, though made with Griftlon meat (a large mountain bird) instead of rabbit. During the meal, Aarely revealed that his deity had sent him a sign: the group needed to leave the monastery as soon as possible.

Ray, meanwhile, made his way to the post office. There, he befriended the postal worker Matteo and struck a deal, informing Sir Halden about the mysterious letters he had been receiving and agreeing to write Matteo about the outcome.

After searching the entire monastery without success, Marvers entered the main hall, where he spoke with Berta. From her, he learned that Layla may have already been healed and released. He also uncovered grim historical knowledge: roughly 150 years ago, Queen Cyria Powsky ordered the eradication of all remaining dragons, resulting in a widespread witch hunt situation in which any being suspected of being a dragon was executed. 
When the group finally reunited, Aarely informed Marvers that Layla was in the Darkroom and infected. He instructed Ray to leave with the group, promising to deliver the priests reply as soon as possible.

On their way to the gate, Marvers put on his armor, revealing the King’s family crest once worn by Lacrima’s soldiers. The group quickly concealed it with Marvers scarf before proceeding. At the gate, they encountered Virex Halden, who offered to let them leave the village in exchange for interrogating them. As part of the deal, they were also to report what they had witnessed to a nearby Lacriman outpost.

Each member of the party was asked the same question. Afterward, Virex released them, just as Aarely arrived. He warned them quietly:

“Be careful. I hope to see you again soon. She who watches me from afar has shown me that no good comes from sharing the whole truth with those who serve Lacrima. Not telling is not lying. Be careful out there.”

And with that, the party made their way onward.
